title: Time-slab prerender & summarization pipeline for low-power multi-series charts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: High-density multi-series time-series charts cause excessive repaint/DOM churn on low-power devices (mobile & low-spec laptops). Screen reader consumers get overwhelmed by per-point announcements when using hover probes or live updates. Goal: Introduce a layered strategy that prerenders time 'slabs' (coarse tiles) and computes lightweight summarization for SR and overview UX so we can reduce main-thread work, DOM nodes, and verbose a11y announcements without degrading interaction accuracy for focused probes.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas prerendering creates 250ms–1s slabs and reduces main-thread paint time by >=30% on representative low-power devices (measured via lighthouse emulation)
Overview thumbnail uses server/client aggregated tile and renders <10 DOM elements for >1k points per series
Screen-reader summary generator provides concise 2–3 phrase summaries on focus with no more than one live-region update per user interaction
Keyboard focus & probe navigation continue to announce precise point-level values when explicitly focused (no loss of fidelity on direct engagement)
Design tokens for color/contrast and focus outline are defined and mapped to existing theme tokens; QA checklist added for WCAG 2.1 AA
design_notes: We will add two new semantic tokens: chart-slab-bg and chart-slab-accent to centralize background and highlight strokes for prerendered tiles
Prefer off-main-thread compositing where possible (OffscreenCanvas) and fall back to a minimal canvas rendering path on unsupported browsers
Summarizer will synthesize an aggregate phrase (e.g., '3 series, median trend rising, range 12–84') rather than read raw point counts
Keep hover/tooltips lightweight: render HTML tooltip shell + canvas snapshot image for preview; only inject DOM text when user interacts via keyboard or requests details
Avoid per-point DOM nodes; use pointer hit-testing in canvas and expose an ARIA-compliant hidden form control that maps current focus to a concise live summary
decisions: Use slab size of 1s (configurable) as default; allow product to override based on dataset density
Server-side micro-aggregation for initial overview tiles (reduces client CPU and bandwidth for first paint)
Implement a coalescing live-region that batches announcement content and limits to one update per 400ms of continuous input
Fallbacks: if OffscreenCanvas unavailable, fallback to requestAnimationFrame-batched canvas rendering with reduced sample-rate
Color mapping: reuse semantic tokens from design system to ensure color-contrast parity across themes; avoid introducing new raw color values
